keyFindings.description: Fast-follow, and the one finding of this round worth acting on: no test pins the per-object repeat rule. The 'a repeated piece' fixture sets the message's own text and the attachment's title, text and fallback all to 'Build failed', so takeOwn puts that string in ownWords and take rejects every attachment piece before slackWalkObject's tally is reached. I checked it by mutation rather than by reading: deleting `|| slices.Contains(yielded, text)` from normalize.go:1304 leaves the whole 39-case TestSlackDeliveredText table green. With that rule gone an attachment carrying title = text = fallback and no own text would deliver its line three times, which is a doubled word in a shape Slack sends — the behaviour is right today and nothing would catch its removal. The remedy is one character: set that fixture's own text to "", leaving its expected summary and delivered text unchanged, since the next fixture already covers suppression against the message's own words.

Recorded by the architect's ruling of 2026-10-25T08:07:14Z. slackWalkFallback wraps visit once per enclosing fallback-carrying object, so a chain of them makes each piece pass through one closure per level above it. The tester measured 1.44 s at 9,900 levels in a 373 KB body against 0.089 s on round 5's listener. My own worst reproduction was cheaper — a 9,900-level chain whose every level carries a distinct fallback, 286,220 B, 59 ms; the same chain with one repeated fallback, 237,839 B, 9 ms; three such chains, 713,173 B, 31 ms — so I could not reach the tester's figure with the shapes I built and record both numbers as measured by whoever measured them. Reaching the shape at all needs an object carrying fallback nested inside another, which Slack does not produce: attachments do not nest and no block kind carries the name. The bound is seconds inside a 10 s write timeout, not round 3's 85 s. What would close it: one tally consulted per piece instead of a closure per enclosing fallback.

Recorded by the same ruling: the rule keys on the name fallback rather than on being an attachment, so a block carrying that name would get the same treatment. No Slack block carries it, so the changelog's 'an attachment's fallback' is true of every message Slack sends.

Fast-follow, unchanged from round 4: slackWalkKeys drops every string under a non-display name, so a context element carrying only a link's url delivers nothing — 'Runbook:' arrives without https://run.book/x. The one string Slack renders that the walk is structurally unable to reach.

Security[prompt], recorded and with the human, unchanged this round. Slack attaches a link unfurl by editing the message, so a crawled page's title and text arrive as message_changed on a person's message carrying user_id and no bot_id, reach payload.text, and session.go appends the payload to the wake prompt after 'Message:'. Two corrections stand from round 4, both read from code: the Legion controller is not on this path, since slackKind returns 'mention' only for event.type app_mention and an unfurl edit is 'message', so the controller's .mention subscription never receives it and its bot_id guard is not bypassed but never reached; and the delimiter is JSON string encoding, which holds, so injected text cannot forge the prompt's own Summary, Message or Topic lines and the residual risk is instruction-shaped text inside the quoted region. The exposed population is any session subscribed to a channel's .message topic. Also still live from round 1: fallback and a button's value are strings Slack renders to nobody. OWASP LLM01 and LLM06, ASVS v5.0.0-1.3.3.

It verified that said is a fresh local per call supplied only to this object's own subtree, so a sibling outside it cannot set it and a nested fallback's own yield still reaches enclosing wrappers; that early termination is preserved, since the wrapper returns the downstream result unchanged and 'said || visit(fallback)' never swallows a false; that the eight-name rank and the per-object tally are otherwise untouched and a non-string fallback enters the alphabetical tail; that slackOwnWordsOnly still answers correctly under deferral; that the cap still distinguishes an exact fit from a truncation; and that message_changed, message_deleted, files, attachment_count, thread_broadcast and app_mention are unmoved, with previous_message never walked. It also traced the consumers — session.go, envoy-client's delivery renderer, pi-envoy and claude-envoy — and found the dedupe key, topics and routing unchanged.
